project.name: rag-code-library-production-structure
project.objective: Build a production-ready RAG Code Library: reusable, tested Python RAG components, the ragkit CLI, canonical manifests, and a local cookbook website. AI authors production code; human reviews and requires independent verification.

lifecycle.next_action: Review completed work and choose the next bounded outcome.

plan_approval.reason: V2 task graph approved. Ten tasks V2-T01 to V2-T010 cover FR-36 to FR-57, NFR-14 to NFR-18 and AC-21 to AC-32 with zero uncovered requirements. Five components are added inside existing categories so no manifest schema change is needed; the orchestration layer injects stages as callables rather than importing component modules, preserving the AST-asserted selectability property. Medium-risk tasks T05, T07, T08 and T09 carry independent-review gates satisfied under the standing delegation in DECISION-c6b1521b.

approval.reason: V2 spine approved as written. 107 requirements checked with no gaps and no duplicates: FR-1 to FR-57, NFR-1 to NFR-18, AC-1 to AC-32. The V2 increment covers document discovery, document loading, chunk validation, chunk deduplication, indexing, index verification and orchestration (FR-36 to FR-57), plus three closures of v1 partials that block v2.md 5.6 and 5.7 (FR-55 normalization documentation mismatch, FR-56 protected system metadata, FR-57 dead retry configuration). Observability, integrations, versioning beyond the index fingerprint, near-duplicate matching, DOCX, Qdrant/pgvector and lifecycle management are explicitly out of scope and must be reported as such under NFR-18 and AC-32.

assumptions.text: The shipped examples keep embedding model and vector-store provider neutral: no default provider or model is selected on the human's behalf. Settings for provider/model/dimensions deliberately have no defaults, matching components/config/settings.py.

invariants.text: Every filesystem write reachable from the ragkit CLI must pass through the single validated path-safety module. It rejects traversal, project-root escape, and symlink escape. No component or command may write outside the resolved destination project.

Component metadata has exactly one canonical source: the component manifest.json validated against schemas/component-manifest.schema.json. The CLI, tests, and cookbook generator all read it; no component definition is duplicated by hand.

decisions.title: Components may split into selectable sub-components
decisions.text: A component area can be divided into sub-components so the human chooses the implementation at add time. Example: ingestion/pdf_extraction splits into sub-components such as pymupdf extraction and ocr extraction, each with its own manifest, README, example and tests, all under components/ingestion/pdf_extraction/. The registry, ragkit list/info/add and the cookbook must support this grouping without forcing a single provider. Categories stay the 15 areas from master.md.

decisions.title: Canonical CLI name is ragkit
decisions.text: ragkit is the canonical CLI name (resolves discovery finding F-5, closed Q-1). pyproject.toml already declares the ragkit entry point. Any doc or scaffold note referring to raglib is stale and must be updated to ragkit.

decisions.title: v1 scope is the core pipeline path
decisions.text: v1 delivers real, tested implementations for: chunking (fixed_size, recursive, token_based, markdown_aware, structure_aware), embeddings (protocol, local, remote, batch), storage (document_store, vector_store_protocol, adapters), retrieval (dense, sparse, hybrid, metadata_filter, result_normalizer), reranking (cross_encoder, relevance_ranking), context (token_budget, context_selector, citation_formatter), config (already done), plus security (input_validation, metadata_validation, retrieved_content), ingestion (pdf_extraction split into sub-components, text_normalizer) and evaluation (retrieval_metrics, answer_metrics, evaluation_dataset). Deferred to v2, recorded as non-goals: observability area, generation LLM providers beyond a config-driven prompt builder, integrations adapters area, hosted cookbook.

decisions.title: Dependency policy: pydantic core, heavy libraries behind sub-components
decisions.text: Runtime core declares pydantic and pydantic-settings only (already in pyproject.toml). Third-party libraries such as pymupdf, OCR engines, rank_bm25, sentence-transformers, cross-encoder models and vector store clients are never imported at module top level by shared code. Each such capability ships as its own sub-component manifest so the human picks it at ragkit add time; its module raises a clear ImportError naming the missing package. No optional-extras indirection is required in v1.

decisions.title: Distribution: personal local use only
decisions.text: The library is consumed by the human on this machine via a local uv environment. No PyPI publishing, no hosted backend, no semver/public API stability commitment in v1. Cookbook website is local static files opened from disk.

decisions.title: U2 RESOLVED: core-types ships as a component with transitive dependency resolution
decisions.text: Shared dataclasses and protocols (Chunk, ScoredDocument, Context, and the chunking/embedding/vector-store/document-store/reranker/context-builder/metric protocols) ship as the core-types component. ragkit add resolves and copies required component dependencies before the requested component. It detects dependency cycles, missing dependencies, and version conflicts and reports each clearly. It never silently installs packages. Component dependency edges reference component ids, never package names.

decisions.title: U3 RESOLVED: manifest schema fields are required and all 31 existing manifests migrate
decisions.text: New manifest fields (required packages with version constraints, optional packages with version constraints, min/max supported Python versions, external services and required environment variables, human-readable install instructions, dependency-missing error text, lifecycle status) are REQUIRED. All 31 existing manifests are migrated in one coordinated change. No silent defaults are introduced for dependency declarations.

decisions.title: U1 RESOLVED: AI authors production-grade implementation code
decisions.text: The human authorizes and requires the agent to author production-quality code for the approved scope: configuration, infrastructure, schemas, CLI, RAG components, security, and evaluation. Production-grade is defined as standalone, reusable, validated, testable code with explicit inputs, stable outputs, controlled failures, and minimal unnecessary coupling. The human reviews changes and requires independent verification through tests and acceptance gates. This supersedes DECISION-ba2975b0, retained for auditability.

decisions.title: U4 RESOLVED: generation ships prompt-builder and grounded-answer-contract in v1
decisions.text: v1 includes both network-free generation components: prompt-builder and grounded-answer-contract. Their interfaces, citation behavior, failure handling, documentation, and tests are specified and implemented. No LLM provider clients are introduced in v1.

decisions.title: U6 RESOLVED: .gitignore restored with real ignore rules
decisions.text: The placeholder one-line .gitignore was replaced with real rules covering virtualenvs, __pycache__ and bytecode, pytest/mypy/ruff caches, build and dist output, egg-info, secrets and .env files, local data and temp files, Genesis local traces, and editor/OS noise. Verified that no required source file is hidden: git status --ignored shows ignored entries only for caches, and the untracked set is now source and spec files only. This fixes the input-manifest pollution that would otherwise make every gate report source-mutated, because inputManifest uses git ls-files --others --exclude-standard and 32 untracked __pycache__ directories existed.

decisions.title: AUTHORIZED EXCEPTION: one hand-edit to .genesis/project.json to add tests/unit/test_registry.py to T-05.scope
decisions.text:
Status: accepted. Decided by the human on 2026-10-10 via an explicit choice between four options (amend project.json / rebuild the downstream task graph / leave T-05 blocked / modify genesis.mjs). The human chose the single hand-edit.

Why an exception was needed at all: KNOWLEDGE-fce57cc5 proved T-05 could not be completed as approved. Its mandatory 'registry' gate runs python -m pytest tests/unit/test_registry.py -q, which exits 5 because the file is a 1-line comment stub; writing tests requires editing a git-tracked file that no task's scope covers; checkScope (genesis.mjs:266) rejects it; base_manifest is captured once via '||=' and never refreshed; and scope is writable only by task add during the planning phase. Replacing T-05 under a new id would have stranded T-06, T-07, T-08, T-10 and T-15 (readyTask requires every dependency to be done), which transitively gates all 21 tasks.

What was changed: exactly one JSON array element added to tasks[id=T-05].scope. Verified before and after: JSON still parses; line count went 3336 -> 3337; a Compare-Object diff against project.json.bak-20261010-201541 shows ONLY 'scripts/validate_components.py' gaining a trailing comma plus the new 'tests/unit/test_registry.py' line. Backup kept at .genesis/project.json.bak-20261010-201541. This matches the existing pattern - T-03, T-04, T-10 and T-13 each list their own gate's test file - so the edit corrects an oversight rather than creating a new privilege.

Procedure that must accompany any such edit: editing scope changes the plan hash, so plan status went 'stale' and a plan check + plan approve were required. Naively approving would have auto-activated T-13 (the first ready queued task), handing T-13 a base_manifest captured before T-05's work and permanently poisoning its later checkScope. Prevented by reverting the edit, control requeue T-05 (which needs an approved plan, hence the revert-first order), re-applying the edit, then plan check and plan approve - so T-05 won the activation scan and received a fresh baseline, while T-13 stayed queued with base_manifest unset. Final state verified: plan approved, active_task T-05, exactly one active task, T-13 base_manifest false.

Scope of this authorization: this one field, this once. It does NOT license future hand-edits to project.json; any further need must go back to the human.

decisions.title: Authorized ONE hand-edit amending gate-test scope for all ten remaining affected tasks (T-06, T-07, T-08, T-09a-g)
decisions.text:
Context
-------
After completing T-05, a full audit of every task's executable gates against its scope found the defect that blocked T-05 (KNOWLEDGE-fce57cc5) was not isolated but systematic. Ten tasks declare a mandatory gate of the form 'python -m pytest tests/unit/test_<area>.py -q' while their scope contains only 'components/<area>' -- so the gate's own file was in no task's scope and did not exist on disk.

  T-06  -> tests/unit/test_chunking.py
  T-07  -> tests/unit/test_embeddings.py
  T-08  -> tests/unit/test_storage.py
  T-09a -> tests/unit/test_retrieval.py
  T-09b -> tests/unit/test_reranking.py
  T-09c -> tests/unit/test_context.py
  T-09d -> tests/unit/test_generation.py
  T-09e -> tests/unit/test_security_components.py
  T-09f -> tests/unit/test_ingestion.py
  T-09g -> tests/unit/test_evaluation.py

T-03, T-04 and T-05 were already correct (T-05 only because DECISION-34d9520b amended it). T-10, T-11, T-13 were already correct: their gate files are in their own scope and are created by those tasks.

Why no supported path exists (all verified against genesis.mjs, not assumed)
--------------------------------------------------------------------------
- task add is the only scope writer (line 930) but line 908 rejects a duplicate id, so it cannot amend an existing task.
- task set writes only state/next/blocker/notes/failures/limitations.
- plan reopen (line 818) requires no active task, and T-06 was active.
- No task delete action exists, so delete-and-readd is impossible; and downstream dependencies reference the original ids anyway.
- task.inputs cannot narrow the check: inputManifest (line 150) is git ls-files over the whole repo minus .genesis/, and inputs only add paths to that set.
- Skipping the file is not an option: a gate of 'pytest tests/unit/test_chunking.py' cannot pass when the file is absent.

kiran was asked directly on 2026-10-10 and chose 'Authorize one hand-edit for all 10' over editing genesis.mjs and over stopping.

What was authorized, and its exact limits
-----------------------------------------
A single edit to .genesis/project.json appending one path to the scope array of each of the ten tasks. Nothing else in the file was changed: no gates, requirements, dependencies, outcomes, risks, states or scenarios. Verified afterwards that all ten scopes now contain their gate file, that the other twelve tasks are byte-for-byte unchanged in scope, and that the JSON still parses (22 tasks).

This extends DECISION-34d9520b; it does not reuse or supersede it. That decision waived the no-hand-edit rule exactly once for one field on T-05. This one is a second, separately authorized waiver, scoped to these ten fields, granted after the human saw the full ten-task list rather than a single instance.

Sequence used (same safe order as T-05)
---------------------------------------
1. Backup: .genesis/project.json.bak-scope-20261010 (293608 bytes, identical to the pre-edit file).
2. control requeue T-06 -- so plan approve would re-activate T-06 rather than the first ready queued task, which after a null active_task would have been T-07.
3. Hand-edit via a Node script doing JSON.parse/stringify. PowerShell's ConvertTo-Json was deliberately not used: it truncates deeply nested objects at a default depth and collapses single-element arrays, and this file is 293 KB of nesting.
4. plan check -> '21 tasks cover 68 requirements', problems: [].
5. plan approve --human kiran --reason ... -> re-stamps the hash. This was required because planHash (line 539) includes scope, so the edit made the plan stale, which would fail requireBuild (line 235) at task completion.
6. Verified: phase=build, active=T-06, T-13 still queued with an empty base_manifest, counts 1 active / 6 done / 15 queued, plan status approved.

Residual risk, stated plainly
-----------------------------
The no-hand-edit rule remains in force. A future task whose gate points outside its scope will hit the same wall and must be escalated again, not edited silently -- this authorization is not a precedent for treating project.json as writable. The structural fix would be either a supported scope-amendment command in genesis.mjs or a plan authored with gate files inside scope; neither is done here, and neither was authorized.
decisions.source: T-06 pre-flight audit: compared every task's executable gate paths against its scope after the T-05 scope deadlock recurred

decisions.title: ragkit list/info render in cli.py; info resolves the <id> placeholder
decisions.text:
ragkit list and info are rendered in cli.py, not the registry, and info resolves the <id> placeholder in install.

WHY: T-10's scope is only src/rag_code_library/cli.py and tests/integration/test_cli_list.py. cli.py's T-01 docstring promised the registry would own list/info, but those functions do not exist anywhere, scope cannot be amended through the CLI (genesis task set permits only active->blocked|failed; task add is the only verb taking --scope), and hand-editing .genesis/project.json is forbidden without new authorization.

The registry is still the single source of component metadata (FR-12): cli.py formats fields the registry owns and re-describes none of them. Both commands go through Registry.load, .manifests, .resolve and UnknownComponentError, so a component added to the tree appears in list/info with no further change. cli.py's module docstring was amended to say so.

ALSO: 26 of 35 manifests store a literal "<id>" placeholder in install ("Copy with: ragkit add <id>"). The id IS known at info time, so info resolves it. This is unlike destination's {project_package}, which resolver.py deliberately leaves un-substituted because only ragkit add, against a project the registry has never seen, can fill it in.

FR-14 asks for "example" and "usage notes" that the manifest schema does not carry (no example or notes property). Mapped as: Example = the component's example.py, else .env.example, else a parenthetical pointing at the README; Usage notes = install; Trade-offs = tradeoffs, which 34 of 35 manifests leave unset and are therefore printed as "(not recorded in this manifest)" rather than invented.
decisions.source: SPEC.md FR-12, FR-13, FR-14; PLAN.md T-10

decisions.title: Provenance is a content lookup, not a sidecar record
decisions.text: generator/provenance.py answers 'which component owns this file?' by hashing the file and comparing it against every file the registry declares, rather than by maintaining a .ragkit.json listing what was added. Two constraints decided it. FR-25 and AC-10 require the copies ragkit add writes to be byte-for-byte identical to their sources, so a provenance header cannot be written into the files themselves; and a sidecar record drifts the moment anyone edits a copied file, re-adds with --force, copies a component by hand, or checks out an older revision, leaving a confidently wrong answer at exactly the moment someone is deciding whether to delete a file. The content lookup needs no state, cannot drift, and answers FR-18 for any file however it got there.

decisions.title: ragkit add splits the destination into an import path and a component namespace
decisions.text: The source file lands on the manifest's declared destination path unchanged, because that path is an import location the user will import from and is not the planner's to move. Documentation, tests and manifest.json land beside it in a directory named for the component, e.g. rag/storage/storage-adapters/manifest.json. A flat layout cannot work: storage-adapters and vector-store-protocol both declare the destination directory rag/storage/ and both ship a README.md and a manifest.json, so a single 'ragkit add storage-adapters' would have collided with itself while copying its own dependency. Python modules are named after themselves and tolerate a shared directory; README.md and manifest.json are not. Component ids are schema-constrained to kebab-case, so the namespace is not a traversal vector.

decisions.title: AC-15's human half is verified headlessly and remains owed to the human
decisions.text: AC-15 says the browser checklist -- collapsible sidebar, section contents, component view fields, copy-to-clipboard, search and filter, breadcrumbs -- is verified by recorded human inspection and never by a claim of automated proof. This machine has no desktop browser connected and the browser tool refuses file:// URLs, so the from-disk inspection could not be performed by the agent and no automated substitute is being offered as its equivalent. What the agent did verify, and recorded as evidence rather than as proof of AC-15, is a headless run of the real cookbook/script.js against a minimal DOM stub: all 35 components across all 5 views render without throwing, each component's own description reaches the page, the copy button is present, 175 markdown fields render with no unclosed tables or lists, and search and filter narrow the list to counts that match the manifest data exactly (bm25 to 3, vector store to 2, external-service to 2, optional-packages to 8, no-extra-packages to 25). That catches render-time failures; it does not prove a browser paints them or that the clipboard works from a local file, which is the point AC-15 is actually making.

decisions.title: AUTHORIZED EXCEPTION: one hand-edit to .genesis/project.json moving T-16 ahead of T-14 and T-15
decisions.text:
Status: accepted. Decided by the human on 2026-10-11 via an explicit choice, after the agent corrected a factual error of its own.

Why an exception was needed: the task queue is array-ordered and genesis.mjs has no reorder command (KNOWLEDGE-3169ff03). 	ask add appends to the end of state.tasks, so T-16 landed at index 22, behind T-14 at index 20 and T-15 at index 21. Both commandRun and plan approve select state.tasks.find(t => t.state === 'queued' && readyTask(state, t)) -- the first match in array order -- so execution order is array order and there is no CLI route to change it.

The error being corrected: before adding T-16 the agent told the human 'either way your components still land before T-14 (docs) and T-15 (final sweep)'. That was wrong -- task add appends rather than inserts -- and the human accepted a different option on that basis. The consequence is substantive, not cosmetic: T-15 is the final verification sweep, so running it before T-16 would leave the three new components' AC-4 and AC-13 coverage outside the sweep that exists to prove acceptance criteria; and T-14 documents shipped behavior, so components built after it go undocumented.

Scope of the edit: move the T-16 task object from the end of the tasks array to immediately before T-14. No field of any task changes; no other key changes; no other file is touched. Afterwards the plan is re-checked and re-approved through the CLI, and the resulting array order is verified by reading it back.

This is the fourth and only other authorized hand-edit of this file, following DECISION-34d9520b, DECISION-80d7753e and DECISION-99257208. Do not hand-edit again without fresh authorization.

decisions.title: T-14 completes with scope check failing structurally, verified by hand instead
decisions.text: The doccmds gate itself passed: python scripts/check_documented_commands.py -> 50 passed, 3 manual, 0 failed, exit 0. Genesis's scope check cannot pass for T-14, and this is structural rather than a real violation. T-14.base_manifest was frozen when T-14 was created (2026-10-10T12:29:50Z), before T-16 ran. Task order was then changed by DECISION-703bc019 so T-16 executes first. The scope check therefore diffs the current tree against a snapshot taken before T-16's authorized work existed, and reads every T-16 file as an out-of-scope change by T-14. Committing does not help: the check compares stored file hashes, not git state, so no commit alters the comparison. Verified by hand instead: T-14 created or modified exactly 8 files -- README.md, docs/architecture.md, docs/cli_reference.md, docs/component_authoring.md, docs/security.md, docs/troubleshooting.md, docs/versioning.md, scripts/check_documented_commands.py. No src/, components/, cookbook/ or tests/ file was written; cookbook/data.js remains byte-identical to a fresh build, and pyproject.toml and uv.lock retain their 10-10 mtimes. The checker's own output confirms only in-scope files were read. scope_check is therefore not cited as evidence for this task.

decisions.title: Authorized hand-edit: refresh T-14.base_manifest to current tree
decisions.text: Authorized by kiran after explicit question. checkScope (genesis.mjs:262-268) diffs current file content hashes against task.base_manifest and throws on any changed file outside task.scope. T-14.base_manifest was captured at task creation on 2026-10-10T12:29:50Z. DECISION-703bc019 then moved T-16 ahead of T-14 in the queue, so T-16's authorized work landed on a tree whose T-14 snapshot predated it, and all 16 of those files read as out-of-scope changes by T-14. Committing cannot fix this: the comparison is content-hash based, and git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard returns the same path set whether or not the files are committed. Genesis re-captures base_manifest only at plan approve (genesis.mjs:847) or via ||= at line 245, which never overwrites an existing value, so no built-in path exists. The edit recomputed base_manifest using the same inputManifest function and the same Node hashing as genesis itself rather than reimplementing it in another language, then wrote JSON.stringify(state, null, 2) to match writeJson formatting. Verified surgical: of every differing leaf in project.json, all 24 lie under tasks[21].base_manifest; the other 22 tasks are byte-identical; T-14's state, scope, gates, blocker and created_at are unchanged; and the project, workflow and lifecycle blocks and schema_version are untouched. Post-edit the tree differs from the refreshed baseline in 0 files. Backup at .genesis/project.json.bak-t14-baseline. The gate then ran for real: doccmds exit 0, 50 passed, 3 manual, 0 failed, evidence T-14-doccmds-8d0ab86d.

decisions.title: AC-15's browser checklist is owned by the human, not closed by agent evidence
decisions.text: kiran opened cookbook/index.html from disk in a real browser and reported that it works, and has stated they will handle the UI from here. AC-15 requires a recorded pass/fail against a fixed six-item checklist -- sidebar groups expand and collapse, each section lists the expected components, each component view shows description/code example/dependencies/use cases/trade-offs, the copy-code button places the example on the clipboard, search and filter narrow the list correctly, and breadcrumbs reach every section -- and says it is verified by recorded human inspection, never by a claim of automated proof. decisions.title: T-15 independent review: three verification scripts reviewed and shown able to fail
decisions.text:
Independent review of T-15's three scripts, performed by the agent under DECISION-c6b1521b (human delegated independent-review gates) and reviewed against the human's own inspection of the deliverables.

WHAT WAS REVIEWED
1. scripts/validate_dependencies.py (AC-14). Walks every shipped .py (148 files), parses with ast, and classifies imports as stdlib, local-to-this-repo, core, dev, declared-guarded, transitive, or renamed-on-PyPI. Local detection matters most: `import core_types` inside another component is a sibling file, not a package, and mistaking it for third-party would have produced 44 false findings. Verified able to fail by planting an undeclared `import requests` (caught, exit 1) and an unguarded `import tiktoken` in a component that does declare tiktoken (caught as not-guarded, exit 1). Both probe files restored; the component's 34 tests still pass afterwards.
2. scripts/check_no_secrets.py (AC-17). 12 credential-shape rules plus a SecretStr-unwrap rule; never prints a match, only a redacted excerpt. Verified able to fail by planting a fake AWS key id and an api_key assignment (both caught, exit 1), then removed the probe.
3. scripts/check_deferred_surface.py (AC-19). Confirms observability and integrations exist in the category enum and ship no implementation, example or test, and that no manifest there points at a real file.

REVIEW FINDINGS, RESOLVED DURING THE TASK
- check_no_secrets initially reported 6 findings, 4 of them the script matching its own source. Fixed by excluding the checker's own file: a checker that always reports itself gets ignored.
- It also flagged `components/config/tests/test_config.py:100`, which calls .get_secret_value() to ASSERT that the value is masked. Banning that call everywhere would make AC-17's own mechanism untestable, so the unwrap rule is exempted in test modules only, and shape rules still apply there.
- It flagged `api_key="secret-key"` in an example, a demo placeholder. Rather than raise the threshold, the generic assignment rule now requires a value to mix character classes before reporting; provider-prefixed rules stay strict.
- validate_dependencies flagged `import magic`, the module name for the PyPI package python-magic. Added an explicit rename map; the mapped package must still be declared and the import still guarded, so the map cannot launder an undeclared dependency.

REVIEW FINDINGS, OPEN AND RECORDED RATHER THAN HIDDEN
- tests/unit/test_registry.py still carries two pre-existing ruff findings (RUF100 unused noqa, PLW1510 subprocess.run without check). That file is not in T-15's declared scope and ruff is not one of T-15's gates, so T-15 cannot clear them without exceeding its scope. They remain owed.
- NFR-2 asks a verification report to state interpreter, exit code, collected, passed, failed, collection errors, skipped-with-reason, xfail and deselected as separate lines. The raw gate stdout carries only "2948 passed, 2 skipped". The full NFR-2 report was therefore recorded separately as the t15-verification-report trace event, including both interpreter strings for AC-3 and every skip reason for AC-2.
- Both allowlists in validate_dependencies (TRANSITIVE, IMPORT_PROVIDED_BY) are printed on every run, so an entry added to make a real undeclared dependency pass is visible in the gate output rather than buried.

AC-20: DECISION-0410c7dc states the agent authors production-grade implementation code while the human reviews and requires independent verification. That matches the spec's current rule exactly, and it supersedes DECISION-ba2975b0. No task is in the forbidden position AC-20 describes, so nothing needed blocking.

decisions.title: T-15 post-completion fix to check_no_secrets, and why all six proofs now read stale
decisions.text:
T-15 post-completion fix: check_no_secrets stopped matching its own audit trail.

FACTS, in order.
1. T-15 completed with all six gates passing; `task complete` enforces proofStatus===pass for every mandatory gate, so at 17:40 on 2026-10-11 the proofs were valid.
2. After completion a final verification run showed `python scripts/check_no_secrets.py` exiting 1 on `.genesis/project.json:517`. The match was DECISION-cc6496b8 -- the T-15 independent review -- quoting the literal text `.get_secret_value()` while explaining why test modules are exempt from that rule. Genesis wrote that prose into project.json; the scanner read it back and reported a leak that was a description of the rule, not a use of it. This is the same self-matching class already hit once when the scanner matched its own source.
3. The unwrap rule was narrowed to Python source only, on the ground that a call site exists only in code. The shape rules were deliberately left scanning `.genesis` and every other artifact, because a credential VALUE pasted into a decision record must still be found. That boundary was proven, not asserted: a planted `.py` file calling `.get_secret_value()` inside an f-string was caught (exit 1), and a planted AWS key id inside `.genesis/_probe_secret.json` was also caught (exit 1). Both probes were removed. `check_no_secrets.py` itself was excluded from the scan from the start, since it necessarily contains the patterns it searches for.
4. This edit staled ALL SIX T-15 proofs, not only `secrets`. Reason: inputManifest(repo, task.inputs) with `inputs: []` hashes every non-ignored file in the repository, so any edit anywhere changes the source hash.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG
Inspection shows T-13 (fixtures=stale), T-14 (doccmds=stale) and T-16 (component-tests=stale, validate=stale) are ALL stale too, each bound to a different hash. Staleness after a task closes is the designed consequence of binding proof to the repo as it stood when the proof ran; every subsequent task necessarily moves the repo. It does not mean a gate failed or was never run. `task complete` is the moment the binding is checked, and it passed.

RE-VERIFICATION ON CURRENT SOURCE, with explicit interpreters
- 3.14.5 (C:\Program Files\Python314\python.exe): 2948 passed, 2 skipped, exit 0
- 3.12.14 (.venv\Scripts\python.exe):             2946 passed, 4 skipped, exit 0
- python scripts/validate_dependencies.py:  exit 0
- python scripts/check_no_secrets.py:       exit 0
- python scripts/check_deferred_surface.py: exit 0
No test in the suite references any of the three scripts, so the edit cannot have moved the suite numbers.

WHY T-15 WAS NOT RE-OPENED
Re-binding the proofs is impossible through the CLI: `control resume` refuses terminal tasks (line 1174) and refuses a non-build phase (line 1180), and `task add` requires the approved plan to be reopened first (line 914), which is a human-gated step that rewinds the lifecycle to planning. Reopening the approved plan to repair a hash binding -- when the bound commands all still exit 0 and the binding was invalidated by a disclosed fix inside T-15's own scope -- would cost more than it protects. Recorded instead of silently tolerated.

STILL OPEN: `tests/unit/test_registry.py` carries two pre-existing ruff findings (RUF100, PLW1510). That file is outside every completed task's scope and ruff is no one's gate, so nobody has cleared them. They remain owed.

decisions.title: text-normalizer removes U+00AD, U+FEFF and U+200B
decisions.text:
Deliberate behavior change to a v1 component, recorded under NFR-17 and landing with its test in V2-T07.

WHAT CHANGED: text-normalizer now removes three Unicode format characters it previously kept -- soft hyphen U+00AD, byte-order mark U+FEFF, and zero-width space U+200B -- as a new named rule ('invisible'), reported in result.rules like every other transformation.

WHY: the requirement (FR-55) closes a behavior/documentation mismatch that existed inside the docs themselves. The README comparison table said text-normalizer 'removes' and used a soft hyphen as its worked example of what a PDF hands you, while the README limitations swore 'U+00AD survives' and 'Zero-width characters are left alone'. The behavior matched the second claim, so the document contradicted itself. All three characters are category Cf, not controls, so the existing control rule never saw them; each renders as nothing while defeating an exact match, which for an index is a correctness problem rather than a cosmetic one.

WHAT DELIBERATELY DID NOT CHANGE: U+200D (ZWJ) is excluded and stays excluded -- it joins emoji and grapheme clusters, so removing it changes what the text says rather than how it is spelled, and this component reports repairs instead of reinterpreting content. U+00A0 (no-break space) is also excluded: it is whitespace, and the existing whitespace rule owns it.

DOCUMENTATION: README rules list renumbered to include rule 5, README limitations rewritten (the two retired claims removed), module docstring rules updated, example.py updated and given a runnable demonstration of all four characters.

TEST: 'a test that fails if either side drifts again' is satisfied by three tests that were mutation-verified in both directions -- five deliberate corruptions were injected and each was caught: (1) behavior stops removing, (2) the README rules list contradicts, (3) the README limitations contradict, (4) a retired claim returns, (5) the codepoints go undocumented. The first draft of the documentation test failed only 1 and 4 -- it required SOME passage to mention removal, which let one passage say 'removed' while another said 'left alone', i.e. it would have certified the exact contradiction it was written to prevent. It was strengthened to assert every passage describing a codepoint characterizes it as removed AND none claims it survives. Source files were confirmed byte-identical after every mutation.

decisions.title: metadata-enricher: reserved system_ fields outrank document-supplied metadata
decisions.text:
Deliberate behavior change to a v1 component, recorded under NFR-17 and landing with its test in V2-T07.

WHAT CHANGED: metadata-enricher's merge precedence. Previously merged was built as extracted then system then source, so source won EVERY collision -- including on the reserved system_ keys. A document supplying system_source_path had its value copied straight into merged, the bag that gets stored, making provenance writable by the thing being provenanced. FR-56 requires the opposite.

NEW PRECEDENCE (documented, low to high): extracted < source < system.

WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: the document still wins every field it legitimately owns. If the caller passes title='X' and the document says title='Y', merged still holds 'Y' -- test_source_wins_a_collision_so_its_metadata_is_never_overwritten still passes unchanged, and a new test pins that non-system fields are still the document's to win so the exception cannot swallow the rule it is an exception to.

NOTHING IS HIDDEN: bundle.source still holds the document's attempt verbatim, so a caller can see exactly what the file asserted. What changed is only which value reaches merged. The overrule is also recorded in bundle.omitted with the reason 'reserved system field supplied by the document; the computed value was kept instead', because this component reports what it discards rather than applying it silently. A document whose supplied value happens to AGREE with the computed one is not reported as a conflict -- filing a conflict when the outcome is identical would train a caller to ignore omitted.

TEST: the existing test test_system_fields_cannot_collide_with_a_document_field, which asserted the attacker's system_source_path survived in the comment and left merged unasserted, is replaced by test_a_document_cannot_overwrite_a_computed_system_field asserting merged carries the computed values, source carries the claim, system was never at risk, and omitted reports both overrules. Two further tests were added for the agreeing-value case and for the non-system-field case.

DOCUMENTATION: module docstring gained a 'Why the document does not win system_' section, MetadataBundle.merged and .omitted field docs state the precedence, and the README's 'Source wins a collision, always' invariant was corrected to state the exception and the order.

knowledge.title: core-types and config each define Chunk/SourceDocument - deferred reconciliation, not an accident
knowledge.text:
components/storage/core_types/core_types.py (T-04) defines Chunk, SourceDocument, Metadata, MetadataValue and a frozen+extra=forbid base that are field-identical to components/config/models.py. This duplication is deliberate and was chosen, not overlooked.

Why: config/__init__.py states 'Standalone library components must NOT depend on it (they ship their own models/exceptions)'. core-types must be copyable alone, and importing config would drag the destination app's settings, prompts and error hierarchy behind a type definition. The human was shown this rule after first choosing 'core-types imports from config' and reversed the decision to self-contained.

Deliberate difference: config's Chunk requires chunk_id/document_id/source_name/page_start/page_end; core-types' Chunk makes those optional, because a chunker is invoked as chunk(text, size=..., overlap=...) and cannot know its document. Everything else mirrors config exactly (_NonEmpty, the ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ sha256 pattern, _Frozen == _Contract), so collapsing them later is a rename-free move.

Reconciliation plan (owed by a FUTURE task, not T-04): no task in the approved 21-task graph owns components/config after T-02, so this cannot be fixed inside T-04 - editing components/config would fail checkScope. The intended end state is core-types as the component-layer vocabulary and config importing/re-exporting from it, at which point core-types' Chunk keeps its optional ids. Until then: do not copy both layers into one project and assume the two Chunk classes are interchangeable - they are different classes and isinstance will fail across them. Consequence to revisit: if core-types had declared dependencies:[settings], every later component depending on core-types would transitively pull settings+prompts+errors+enums.

3. checkScope (genesis.mjs:266) compares current digests against task.base_manifest and throws 'changes outside task scope' for any changed path not matching a scope prefix.

T-03 owns test_path_safety.py, T-04 owns test_protocols.py, T-10 owns tests/integration/test_cli_list.py, T-13 owns test_manifest_validation.py - T-05 is the only test-bearing task that omits its own gate's target.

Scope is written in exactly ONE place: task add (genesis.mjs:930, --scope). task set edits only state/next/blocker/notes/failures/limitations. plan reopen only clears plan_check/plan_approval and requires no active task; it does not edit tasks. There is no amend/edit/scope action (the only 'update' is incident update, line 1406).

Rejecting T-05 to recreate it under a new id with corrected scope strands the project: readyTask() requires every dependency to be state==='done', and T-06, T-07, T-08, T-10 and T-15 depend directly on T-05 (T-08 further gates all of T-09a-g; T-10 gates T-11->T-12->T-14). The pattern is ^(?![\\/])(?!.*(?:^|/)\.\.(?:/|$)).*$. Measured behaviour:
  REJECT  '/abs/path.py'        (leading slash) - promised, delivered
  REJECT  '../escape.py'        (.. segment)    - promised, delivered
  REJECT  '\\server\\share\\x.py' (leading backslash) - promised, delivered
  ACCEPT  'C:\\Windows\\Temp\\out.py'  (drive-letter absolute) - promised, NOT delivered
  ACCEPT  'foo/bar\\baz.py'            (interior backslash)   - promised, NOT delivered
  ACCEPT  '..\\..\\escaped\\x.py'      (backslash-style traversal) - promised, NOT delivered, and the .. lookaround only tests for '/' separators

Why it is not a write-time hole: NFR-3 sends every filesystem write through src/rag_code_library/security/path_safety.py, and T-03 proved that SafeDestination rejects absolute-outside-root, drive-letter and UNC targets (tests/unit/test_path_safety.py, 23 tests). So the manifest check is early-warning UX, not the security boundary. The gap still matters because a manifest that validates clean and then fails at add time is exactly the non-actionable sequence FR-11 exists to prevent.

What T-05 does about it: scripts/validate_components.py's own stub comment commits it to checking 'destination safety', so the registry enforces two layers - the schema pattern verbatim (FR-24: validate against the schema) plus a separate repo-level check in registry/validator.py rejecting backslashes anywhere and drive-letter prefixes. The JSON-schema layer is left untouched: the two disagree only by this documented, deliberately stricter rule, and every real manifest satisfies both (32/32 pass).

Not fixed here: correcting the pattern or the description is a change to schemas/component-manifest.schema.json, which belongs to T-02's scope and is closed after plan approval. Whoever owns manifest validation next should decide which side is wrong - tighten the pattern to match the prose, or soften the prose to match the pattern.\
knowledge.source: T-05 pre-flight; probe of schemas/component-manifest.schema.json destination.pattern against six candidate paths

knowledge.title: The schema's destination pattern cannot be a pydantic pattern= constraint: Rust regex has no look-around
knowledge.text:
Found 2026-10-10 during T-05. schemas/component-manifest.schema.json's destination pattern is ^(?![\\/])(?!.*(?:^|/)\.\.(?:/|$)).*\$ -- two negative look-aheads. pydantic compiles StringConstraints(pattern=...) with the Rust regex crate, which does not support look-around, so building a model with that constraint raises SchemaError at CLASS CONSTRUCTION time, i.e. at import. The failure is not a validation error on one bad manifest: it makes the entire module unimportable, so anything that imports the model on the way to doing unrelated work fails too.

Measured: importing src/rag_code_library/registry/manifest.py with pattern=_DESTINATION in the destination annotation dies with 'SchemaError: look-around (e.g. lookahead, lookbehind) is not supported' from pydantic's _model_construction. The other four schema patterns -- id ^[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*\$, version ^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\$, requires_python ^\d+\.\d+\$, package name ^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]*\$ -- all compile fine under Rust regex; only destination uses look-around.

What T-05 does: destination is declared as Annotated[str, StringConstraints(min_length=1)] and the pattern is applied by a field_validator named _destination_is_contained using Python's own re.search. Semantics stay those of JSON Schema, where pattern is an UNANCHORED search; the pattern anchors itself with ^ and \$, so re.search reproduces RegExp.test() exactly. The ValueError raised there is what produces the actionable message 'must be relative to the destination root, use forward slashes, and contain no .. segment; got ...'.

For whoever writes manifest validation next (T-13 owns tests/unit/test_manifest_validation.py): reuse rag_code_library.registry.ComponentManifest rather than re-deriving a model, and do not try to move this rule into a pattern= constraint. FR-3 also means jsonschema is unavailable, so the registry model is currently the only executable form of this schema in the runtime dependency set.

Not a defect in the schema itself -- the pattern is valid ECMA/JSON Schema regex. It is a constraint on which validator can host it.
knowledge.source: T-05 self-review; import failure reproduced while building registry/manifest.py

knowledge.title: The eight invalid_manifests fixtures are deliberately sparse, so each reports its intended corruption plus a cascade of Field-required errors
knowledge.text:
Observed 2026-10-10 while T-05 wired tests/fixtures/invalid_manifests/ into validate_components.py and tests/unit/test_registry.py.

Each fixture was cut down to roughly the field under test rather than being a fully-valid manifest plus one mutation. Consequence: validating one produces the intended signal FIRST and then ~8 further 'Field required' messages for status, requires_python, required_packages, optional_packages, external_services, install and missing_dependency_message.

Example, real output for malformed_version_format.json:
  bad-version-chunker (tests/fixtures/invalid_manifests/malformed_version_format.json): schema violation: version: String should match pattern '^\d+\.\d+\.\d+\$'; status: Field required; requires_python: Field required; required_packages: Field required; optional_packages: Field required; external_services: Field required; install: Field required; missing_dependency_message: Field required

The intended corruption is still there and still first, so the fixtures are sound -- but only if a test asserts on the specific signal, not on the message as a whole.

What T-05 does about it: tests/unit/test_registry.py keeps an explicit CORRUPTIONS table mapping each fixture file to its identifying substring (e.g. malformed_id_pattern.json -> 'id: String should match pattern', path_traversal_destination.json -> 'destination: Value error') and asserts that substring is present, plus len(registry.issues) == 1 so no unrelated check fires. There is also a guard test asserting the CORRUPTIONS keys exactly equal the *.json files on disk, so a fixture cannot be deleted without failing the parametrisation.

Why they are not fixed here: tests/fixtures/invalid_manifests/ belongs to T-13 (gate: fixtures), not T-05. Adding the missing required fields would make each fixture demonstrate exactly one corruption, which is arguably what they should be -- that is T-13's call to make, not a unilateral edit by T-05.

For T-13: if you assert on full output rather than the identifying substring, these fixtures will read as seven unexplained failures per file. Either enrich them to valid-plus-one-mutation, or assert on the signal. Note also that they are named for their corruption (malformed_id_pattern.json), NOT manifest.json, so any discovery helper must match *.json rather than manifest.json -- that is why registry/loader.discover() globs *.json, and the components/ tree contains only manifest.json files so one convention serves both trees.

knowledge.title: sparse-retrieval implements BM25 rather than importing rank-bm25
knowledge.text: The approved SPEC component table lists rank-bm25>=0.2.2 as sparse-retrieval's optional dependency. It is not used, and the manifest now declares no optional packages for that component. Reason: rank-bm25 computes IDF without the +1 smoothing on some paths, so the same corpus scored by the two scorers ranks differently. A retriever whose output depends on which wheels are installed cannot be regression-tested, and T-13/T-15 fixture and full-suite gates would be measuring the environment rather than the code. Okapi BM25 is ~30 lines of fully specified arithmetic with no external state, so implementing it removes the variability at the cost of no BM25+ extensions, no parameter-free variants and no per-field weighting. Deviation is confined to the dependency declaration: the retrieval behaviour the SPEC describes is unchanged, and tests/unit/test_retrieval.py asserts both that results are unaffected by blocking the rank_bm25 import and that the manifest declares no optional packages.

knowledge.title: T-09f review: the image_factory seam was unusable, and two dead/misleading API surfaces removed
knowledge.text: Independent review of the three ingestion components, performed by the agent on the human's standing instruction (2026-10-10: 'do not ask me for code review, do it by your own'). Genesis does not require an independent-review GATE for T-09f: it is risk=low with one mandatory executable gate (genesis.mjs:254 gates review on risk !== 'low'), so this knowledge record is where the findings are kept rather than a gate proof. Four defects in shipped component code were found and fixed: (1) SELF-SHADOWING. PdfExtractor._ensure_fitz did __import__('pymupdf'), which resolved to the COMPONENT ITSELF whenever its own directory sat on sys.path -- a harness and example situation, since in a project the file lands inside a package namespace. The failure surfaced three frames later as 'module pymupdf has no attribute open', wrapped as 'could not be opened as a PDF': a baffling complaint about a document when the real problem was the import path. It now compares module.__file__ against __file__ and raises MissingDependency explaining the shadow. (2) THE OCR SEAM COULD NOT BE USED. OcrExtractor(image_factory=...) stood in for image OPENING only, leaving pytesseract as None, so no OCR could ever run through it. The gate test passed only by assigning extractor._libs directly -- a private arrangement no caller had, which is precisely what a test seam exists to avoid. Replaced with two ORTHOGONAL public seams, image_factory and engine_factory, each of which skips only its own import; substituting half the boundary no longer reports success and still raises MissingDependency. (3) DEAD API SURFACE. ExtractedPage.confidence and OcrResult.mean_confidence were never populated, because pytesseract.image_to_string does not report confidence -- reaching it needs image_to_data, a second pass over every page on the slowest component in the library, and no Tesseract binary has ever been run against this file. Removed rather than shipped as fields that are always None, which read as 'the engine was certain of nothing'; documented as a known limitation. (4) THE ALLOW-LIST REFUSED A REAL LANGUAGE. The language check accepted only alnum, '+' and '-', so it rejected 'chi_sim' -- a genuine Tesseract code, since real codes use underscore. Found by the component's own new test, not by inspection. Underscore added. Also fixed: a gate test that passed on 3.14 only because pillow happens to be installed in user site there (it failed on 3.12) and now substitutes PIL so it is deterministic on both interpreters; and two example bugs, one of which clobbered a real PDF with a stand-in before reading it. Verification: gate 150 passed on 3.14.5 and 149 passed+1 skipped on 3.12.14; full suite 2601 and 2599 passed; both pymupdf examples exit 0 on BOTH interpreters, exercising the real library on 3.14 and the honest MissingDependency fallback on 3.12; OCR example exits 0 on both; 35 manifests valid; scope PASS with 0 outside; AC-13 clean; pyproject.toml and uv.lock untouched. A seeded 16,000-trial fuzz test for idempotence across all four Unicode forms was added to the gate: zero failures, zero second-pass drift.

knowledge.title: Evaluation area: score-vs-gate, no combined metric, and a dataset that computes nothing
knowledge.text: retrieval-metrics, answer-metrics and evaluation-dataset each declare dependencies: [] and define their own error hierarchy, so each copies out alone; none imports a sibling, which is AST-asserted in tests/unit/test_evaluation.py across all nine python files in the area.

knowledge.title: module-name exception checks break under python -m
knowledge.text:
`type(exc).__module__.startswith("<package>")` silently fails when the module raising the error is itself executed as `python -m <package>.<module>`, because runpy then sets that module's __name__ to "__main__", so every class it defines reports __module__ == "__main__".

Hit in src/rag_code_library/cli.py: main() recognised domain errors by that check, which meant every exception cli.py itself raised turned into a raw traceback under `python -m rag_code_library.cli` while working correctly under the installed `ragkit` console script. Only the module running as __main__ is affected - exceptions raised by imported modules (e.g. UnknownComponentError in registry.resolver) keep their real __module__ and were never broken, which is why the bug hid.

Lesson: when classifying exceptions by module, do not use the check on exceptions the module defines itself. Catch them by name instead.

knowledge.title: Registry.get returns None for an unknown id; only resolve() raises
knowledge.text: loader.py defines get() as returning ManifestEntry | None via _by_id.get(), and puts the UnknownComponentError in resolve() instead. Calling registry.get(id).manifest on an id that is not loaded therefore raises AttributeError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'manifest', not the readable 'unknown component X' error the CLI already produces for info. Any new code walking the registry must check for None and raise UnknownComponentError(current, registry.ids) itself to stay consistent. Caught in T-11 when resolve_order traversed a dependency; it surfaced as a raw traceback, which FR-19 forbids.

knowledge.title: Genesis's task queue is array-ordered and cannot be reordered from the CLI
knowledge.text: There is no reorder, move or insert command in genesis.mjs, so a task added with 	ask add is appended to the end of state.tasks and always activates after every earlier queued task. Activation happens in exactly two places: 	ask add (only when no task is active) and plan approve, both of which take state.tasks.find(t => t.state === 'queued' && readyTask(state, t)) -- the first match in array order. commandRun refuses to start when active_task is null ('No active task'), and control pause / 	ask set only accept an already-active task, so there is no way to promote a queued task directly. Consequence: when the human asks for new work to land before a task that is already in the plan, the only ordering that is possible is to complete the earlier task first. The alternative is hand-editing .genesis/project.json, which is forbidden without fresh authorization. Recorded after the human requested three ingestion components before the then-active T-13 and, on being told the constraint, chose to do T-13 first rather than authorize a plan-record edit.

knowledge.title: tests/unit/test_registry.py carries two pre-existing ruff findings, out of scope for T-13
knowledge.text: Found 2026-10-11 while T-13 linted its own new file. uff check tests/unit/test_registry.py reports RUF100 at line 48 (unused # noqa: E402, because E402 is not enabled in this repo's config) and PLW1510 at line 116 (subprocess.run without an explicit check argument). Both predate T-13 and neither is in T-13's declared scope (tests/fixtures/invalid_manifests and tests/unit/test_manifest_validation.py), so they were reported rather than fixed -- fixing them would put T-13 outside its own scope check. PLW1510 is the one with substance: a subprocess whose exit code is not checked can pass silently. T-15's final sweep owns repo-wide lint, so this is where they should be cleared. Also recorded because the RUF100 pattern recurs across the repo's test files, each of which carries a redundant noqa for the same reason.

knowledge.title: task add cannot set scope or scenarios, so T-16's scope is empty and its scope check passes trivially
knowledge.text:
Observed 2026-10-11 while starting T-16. genesis task add accepts only --id, --outcome, --requirement, --risk and --gate; there is no --scope or --scenario flag, and 	ask set permits only active -> blocked|failed. A task added this way therefore has scope: [] and scenarios: []. Consequence: scope_check.mjs reports 'changed 0, OUTSIDE SCOPE 0, SCOPE CHECK: PASS' for T-16 regardless of what is edited, because there is no scope to compare against. It is a vacuous pass, exactly the class of gate that KNOWLEDGE-fce57cc5 flagged for T-05 -- so for T-16 the intended scope was declared by hand and self-enforced instead: components/ingestion/file_type_validator/**, components/ingestion/document_identity_resolver/**, components/ingestion/metadata_enricher/**, plus cookbook/data.js (see the coupling below).

Second finding, same session: adding a component forces an edit outside the new task's own area. scripts/build_cookbook.py enumerates every registry component, so a new manifest makes the committed cookbook/data.js stale and fails T-12's  uild gate and NFR-6's no-drift rule. Regenerating data.js is therefore mandatory inside T-16, not optional and not deferrable to T-15 -- leaving it stale would ship a known-failing gate.

knowledge.title: CORRECTION: an empty task scope makes scope_check FAIL, not pass -- see KNOWLEDGE-13918e6b
knowledge.text:
KNOWLEDGE-13918e6b recorded on 2026-10-11 that T-16's empty scope makes scope_check.mjs 'pass trivially'. That was wrong, and it was wrong in a dangerous direction. Measured while T-16 had edits on disk: with scope [] and 16 changed files, scope_check reports 'changed 16, OUTSIDE SCOPE 16, SCOPE CHECK: FAIL'. The reason the earlier observation seemed to confirm a vacuous pass is that it was run before any file had been touched -- changed was 0, so there was nothing to place outside a scope. Any task with an empty scope and any edit at all fails.

Practical consequence: a task added with genesis task add (which has no --scope flag) cannot pass scope_check no matter what it does, including doing exactly the right work. So scope_check is not evidence either way for such a task and must not be cited as one. The discipline it normally supplies has to be replaced by hand: state the intended scope explicitly, then verify by reading back the changed-file list and confirming every entry is expected.

Verified that way for T-16: the 16 changed files were the five files of each new component (README.md, the module, example.py, manifest.json, tests/test_component.py) plus cookbook/data.js, which is not optional -- scripts/build_cookbook.py enumerates every registry component, so a new manifest makes the committed data.js stale and fails both T-12's  uild gate and NFR-6. Nothing outside that set was touched, and pyproject.toml and uv.lock kept their 10-10 mtimes.

knowledge.title: Every task created on 10-10 fails scope check after the task reorder; T-15 will too
knowledge.text: All tasks were created 2026-10-10, so every one of them holds a base_manifest captured before T-13, T-14 and T-16 did their work. Because DECISION-703bc019 put T-16 ahead of T-14 ahead of T-15, each later task inherits a snapshot that predates the earlier task's output. Expect T-15's genesis run to stop with scope-violation listing T-14's docs and scripts/check_documented_commands.py as outside its scope. The fix is the same authorized base_manifest refresh, and it must be verified surgical each time: recompute with genesis's own inputManifest, assert every differing leaf stays under that task's base_manifest, assert the other tasks and the project/workflow/lifecycle blocks are untouched, and back up first. Do not treat a failing scope check here as evidence of a real violation, and do not cite it as evidence for or against the task. Also note the task completes only after the gate is recorded: genesis task complete refuses with 'cannot complete T-14; doccmds:pending' until genesis run has executed the gate and written its evidence file, so running the gate manually with python is not sufficient on its own.

knowledge.title: PATH python now resolves to the 3.12 venv, and every completed task reads stale gates by design
knowledge.text:
Two traps found while finishing T-15; both cost real time and both will recur.

TRAP 1 -- `python` on PATH stopped meaning the host interpreter.
After a session restart the shell resolves `python` to `.venv\Scripts\python.exe` (3.12.14). Before the restart it resolved to `C:\Program Files\Python314\python.exe` (3.14.5). Nothing in the repo changed; the shell's PATH did. Consequence: a bare `python -m pytest -q` silently reports the 3.12 numbers while looking like the host run. Always pin the interpreter when a result is evidence:
  C:\Program Files\Python314\python.exe -m pytest -q      -> 2948 passed, 2 skipped
  .venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pytest -q                   -> 2946 passed, 4 skipped
Do not trust `$LASTEXITCODE` after a PowerShell pipeline either: `x | Select-Object` resets it, which made a failing `import pymupdf` read as success twice in one command. Capture into a variable immediately, or run via `cmd /c` for exit codes.

TRAP 2 -- completed tasks show `stale` gates; that is the design, not a failure.
`proofStatus` compares the proof's recorded source_hash against `digest(inputManifest(repo, task.inputs))`. inputManifest hashes every non-ignored file (excluding .genesis), and tasks here have `inputs: []`, so the hash is whole-repo. Any later commit stales every earlier task's proofs. Observed: T-13 fixtures=stale, T-14 doccmds=stale, T-15 all six=stale, T-16 component-tests+validate=stale -- each bound to a different hash, i.e. the repo as it was when that gate ran. The binding is checked at `task complete` (mandatory gates must read pass), not continuously afterwards. Never treat `stale` as `failed`, and never re-open an approved plan just to refresh a binding you cannot refresh through `control resume` (terminal tasks are refused) without first confirming the bound commands still exit 0.

Related, for interpreting counts: the interpreter is identifiable from the numbers alone here, because pymupdf is installed for 3.14.5 but not for the 3.12 venv. 2948/2 means 3.14.5; 2946/4 means 3.12.14; the total stays 2950 either way and the delta is exactly the two pymupdf tests.

knowledge.title: V2 gap analysis: 20 ingestion steps against current source -- 0 complete, 12 partial, 8 missing
knowledge.text:
V2 GAP ANALYSIS (v2.md's 20 ingestion steps vs. current source). Verified in code and tests, not README claims. Repo is a component library: 38 manifests, 11 categories, 0 registry issues.

TALLY: 0 complete, 12 partial, 8 missing. Plus cross-stage orchestration = missing.

MISSING (no implementation at all)
- Step 1 Document Discovery: only rglob is the CLI finding manifests (cli.py:124). No directory walker, no extension/exclusion config, no added/modified/deleted detection, no discovery records, no source adapters.
- Step 4 Document Loading: no loader interface exists. Two PDF-only extractors, and their result shapes differ (pymupdf.py:120 pages: tuple[str] vs ocr.py:138 pages: tuple[ExtractedPage]). No DOCX/HTML/Markdown/plain-text loader. OCR refuses PDFs (ocr.py:300-319).
- Step 9 Chunk Validation: no chunk validator. Whitespace-only chunks pass both the chunker guard (fixed_size_chunker.py:89 tests only `not self.text`) and embedding's validate_texts (embedding_protocol.py:148). No severity model, no reject/repair/quarantine policy, no failure records.
- Step 10 Chunk Deduplication: none. Only query-time passage dedup in context_selector.py:118-206, which runs at retrieval, not ingestion.
- Step 12 Indexing as a step: adapter primitives only. document-store has NO backend (nothing calls put()); only Chroma+Faiss, no Qdrant/pgvector; no upsert/update (Chroma uses .add, Faiss leaks stale labels on re-add); no bounded batches; _serialise drops page_start/page_end and index_fingerprint.
- Step 13 Index Verification: nothing. Only count() at storage_adapters.py:335, and Faiss's count can include stale rows.
- Step 17 Observability: no logging anywhere in the repo (grep import logging|getLogger|structlog|loguru = 0). No counters, timers, correlation ids, run summaries.
- Step 20 Lifecycle: change detection exists (DocumentIdentityResolver) but is in-memory and per-instance. No deletion policy, no document->chunk-id mapping for removal, no tombstones, no retention, no audit, no reference counting for shared chunks.

PARTIAL (real behavior, specific gaps)
- Step 2 File Validation: content-based ID, configurable max_bytes checked pre-read, empty/oversized/renamed/corrupt covered by tests. Missing: structured failure result (failures are exceptions only), no rejected-vs-transient flag, nothing records reasons, nothing enforces "rejected files do not reach extraction", ZIP sniff only (a 10-byte %PDF file passes).
- Step 3 Document Identification: sha256[:32], source-vs-content split, rename policy, filename-independent duplicate detection, all tested. Missing: history is per-instance in-memory, no newer-version protection, duplicate provenance is just paths, no cross-process duplicate detection.
- Step 5 Text Extraction: per-page text, typed errors, no invented text. Missing: page numbers as fields, headings/tables/lists, source offsets for citations, per-page warnings vs failures (one bad page aborts all), empty-page vs failed-page distinction, mixed text+image docs, configurable OCR fallback.
- Step 6 Text Normalization: 4 config knobs, original retained, rules reported, provened idempotence incl. a 16k fuzz test. Missing: encoding defects (U+FEFF/U+00AD/U+200B NOT removed despite text_normalizer.py:13 and README:23 claiming they are -- a doc/behavior bug), no configurable artifact rules, no repeated header/footer normalization (needs page boundaries it never receives), no material-alteration threshold.
- Step 7 Metadata Enrichment: three-bag separation, no invented values, drop-with-reason. Missing: document_id/source type/filename-vs-format/section/doc version/parser identity absent; merged.update(source) runs LAST so document metadata overwrites system_* (tests/test_component.py:105-118 asserts the attacker value stays); no enforced schema; metadata never propagates into chunks (chunkers emit metadata={}). The "source wins always" precedence directly conflicts with v2.md's protected-system-field rule.
- Step 8 Chunking: 5 strategies, size+overlap, per-strategy caps, oversized table/code handling, no empty chunks, tiktoken optional, strong boundary tests. Missing: sentence-aware and semantic strategies; document_id/source_name/offsets are always None and tests assert None; chunk_id defaults None; no parent-child; make_chunk_id exists at config/models.py:42 but no pipeline ever calls it.
- Step 11 Embedding: protocol + 3 providers + batching + dimension/shape/finite validation + no-default remote + never silently omits. Missing: NO retry at all (grep time.sleep/for attempt = 0), EmbeddingSettings.max_retries is dead config nothing reads, HTTP 429 raises immediately (remote_embeddings.py:222), no embedding cache/reuse, index_fingerprint never computed/stored/compared.
- Step 14 Failure Handling: error taxonomy with stage/retryable/code/details exists and is tested (config/errors.py:23-115, is_retryable). But NOTHING acts on it -- no retry loop exists anywhere. No resume, no quarantine, no failed-vs-pending ledger, no termination handling. PartialFailure exists only for ragkit add file copying.
- Step 15 Idempotency: stable ids and index_fingerprint exist as DATA. Missing the executor: no stage-state record, no skip-if-unchanged driver, no write-side upsert, no load-time fingerprint comparison, no concurrent-ingest policy.
- Step 16 Versioning: manifest "version": "0.1.0" is COMPONENT MATURITY, explicitly not processing-config version (docs/versioning.md:14). index_fingerprint hashes config but nothing persists or compares it. Missing: parser version, normalization version, metadata schema version, index/collection version, controlled rebuild, last-known-good preservation.
- Step 18 Testing: 18 unit files, 118 component test files, 7 integration, adapter contract tests, 7 hostile manifest fixtures. Missing layers required by v2: dedup, idempotency, failure-recovery, end-to-end ingestion (no pipeline exists to exercise), regression corpus for these bugs.
- Step 19 Security: strong -- path_safety (NFR-3), input-validation, metadata-validation, retrieved-content, hostile fixtures, check_no_secrets, SecretStr. Gaps: IngestionSettings declares max_file_size_bytes/max_pages/max_total_chars (settings.py:44-51) but enforcement is partial; no documented suspicious-document policy; no prompt-injection claim should be made from a detector alone.

CROSS-STAGE B ORCHESTRATION: nothing. ragkit has exactly three subcommands -- list, info, add (cli.py:63-102). src/rag_code_library/commands/ does not exist. components/config/__init__.py:3 explicitly assigns orchestration to the consumer.

CROSS-STAGE A/C/D/E: core_types pydantic contracts exist and are reused; Settings groups cover ingestion/chunking/embedding/storage/retries; core deps are only pydantic+pydantic-settings; no LangChain/LlamaIndex. These are in good shape.

BLOCKERS / DECISIONS NEEDED FROM THE HUMAN
1. Step 17 collides with v1: DECISION-64826fc4 and scripts/check_deferred_surface.py (a T-15 gate) require observability and integrations to ship NO code. Implementing Step 17 fails that gate. Lifting the deferral is a human product decision.
2. SPEC.md is the approved v1 spec (68 requirements). v2.md needs its own identifiers and approvals; the plan is locked and would need `plan reopen`.
3. Scope: 8 missing + 12 partial including a full orchestrator is a second project. v2.md 4.B warns against introducing a large workflow framework for abstraction alone.

knowledge.title: V2 architecture: components are import-isolated, so the pipeline injects stages instead of importing them
knowledge.text:
V2 ARCHITECTURE CONSTRAINT, verified before writing the V2 requirements.

FACTS.
1. Components import neither each other nor `rag_code_library`. Only ONE `__init__.py` exists under components/ (components/config/__init__.py); every other component is a bare module loaded by `sys.path.insert(0, parents[1])` in its own tests (e.g. components/ingestion/file_type_validator/tests/test_component.py:20) and example.py (same pattern).
2. `src/rag_code_library` does NOT import any component module. Its only references to "components" are the tree locator `_components_root()` (cli.py:114-127) and display strings.
3. The cross-component import ban is AST-asserted, not stylistic: tests/unit/test_ingestion.py:651 `_imported()` walks the AST, and test_neither_sub_component_imports_the_other asserts pdf_extraction_pymupdf does not import ocr and vice versa. knowledge.title: RetryPolicy needs a call-site classifier for component error types
knowledge.text:
RetryPolicy (components/config/retry.py, added in V2-T07 for FR-57) does not classify errors itself: it defers to config.is_retryable, which returns False for any exception type it does not own.

Consequence for whoever wires retry into the pipeline (V2-T08): wrapping a component call in RetryPolicy.call(fn) with the DEFAULT retry_if will not retry it. The embedding components raise embedding_protocol.EmbeddingProviderError and EmbeddingInputError; these are NOT RagError subclasses, by design, because components import neither config nor each other.

The default is deliberately conservative and should stay that way. BatchEmbedder reports both a permanent validation failure ('1 vector(s) for 2 input(s)', a width mismatch) and a transient provider failure (wrapped RuntimeError, e.g. HTTP 429) as the SAME type, EmbeddingProviderError. No default rule could separate them, so classifying is inherently a call-site decision -- only the caller knows whether the provider said "later" or "never".

So the orchestration layer must pass retry_if explicitly when wrapping a component call. Proven, not asserted: tests/unit/test_embeddings.py::test_a_component_error_is_not_retried_unless_the_call_site_says_so drives a provider that fails 99 times through RetryPolicy with the default classifier and asserts exactly one attempt.

Retry is deliberately NOT inside any component: components must stay independently copyable and must not grow control flow their settings cannot reach (pre-flight note on V2-T07).

tasks.outcome: Ship a chunk-validator component carrying rule id, severity and reason, with an explicit reject, repair or quarantine policy
tasks.next_action: Pre-flight. A whitespace-only chunk must be detectable, which the current chunkers do not flag.
notes: A test caught a genuine inconsistency in the component, not in the test: ValidationResult reported chunk_id='' while simultaneously filing MISSING_CHUNK_ID for it. An empty string is not an identifier the chunk 'has', so inspect() now normalises blank ids to None, making the result consistent with its own finding.

The 'accepted is safe' invariant is checked by RE-INSPECTING every accepted chunk rather than by trusting the run's own bookkeeping. That matters under REPAIR: results[] records the PRE-repair findings (which is what repairs[] documents), so only a fresh inspection can prove the accepted set is clean. The first draft of the helper asserted on counts instead and would have passed while a repaired chunk was actually still broken.

The import-discipline test initially grepped for the phrase 'core_types', which failed on the module's own DOCSTRING mentioning it. Replaced with an AST walk asserting the module imports only sys.stdlib_module_names -- a real dependency check rather than a substring check.
limitations: This validator reads chunks by ATTRIBUTE only; it never validates a chunk against the pydantic schema in core-types. Schema-level constraints (field types, max_length, enums) are therefore not enforced here, and a chunk that passes validation can still fail model construction downstream.

extraction-anomaly fires only on the explicit marker keys in anomaly_markers (extraction_warning, extraction_failed, ocr_failed). A chunker recording extraction problems under any other name will not be detected, and this component deliberately does not guess.

Size bounds are measured by size_of, which defaults to len -- so they are CHARACTERS, not tokens. The caller must pass a token counter when token accuracy matters. No cross-chunk checks are made: duplicate and overlapping content is chunk-deduplicator's job.

Only three rules are repairable (missing-chunk-id, invalid-chunk-id, and an INVERTED page range), because only those are derivable from the chunk itself. A page range below 1, an oversized chunk, or empty text is held rather than guessed at -- held, never dropped, so no chunk can vanish without a recorded reason.

tasks.outcome: Ship a chunk-deduplicator with deterministic content hashing, preserved provenance, and fingerprint-gated embedding reuse
tasks.next_action: Pre-flight. Near-duplicate similarity matching is explicitly out of scope and must not be claimed.
notes: A test-writer error exposed a real component defect: differences() iterated hard-coded attribute names ('chunking') while the field is named chunking_hash, and check() then did getattr(recorded, name) using the LABEL rather than the attribute. Caught by running the example, which is exactly what it is for. Replaced both with one module-level _FINGERPRINT_FIELDS tuple of (attribute, label) pairs so the two can never drift apart again.

The 'accepted' invariant is stated as a refusal list rather than a happy path: test_the_gate_does_not_silently_reuse_across_a_long_pipeline_run walks five pipeline steps and asserts each non-matching one returns False. Silent reuse is the failure mode that costs weeks to notice, so it is asserted directly instead of being implied by a passing case.
limitations: EXACT content equality only. Near-duplicate similarity matching -- cosine, MinHash, shingling, token overlap -- is NOT implemented and must not be claimed (FR-43). A corpus of paraphrases, or text differing in one word or in letter case, is reported as having no duplicates. This is a deliberate boundary, not a gap to be papered over: folding case or ignoring small differences would make this component claim a judgement about meaning that it does not compute.

Only the chunk TEXT is hashed. Metadata is not part of the comparison and is NOT merged from a removed duplicate into its survivor, so a duplicate carrying richer metadata -- a different section anchor, a distinct startLine -- has that metadata dropped from the index. The Appearance record preserves document_id, source_name, chunk_id and chunk_index, so the CONTENT is always attributable afterwards, but the metadata of a removed copy is not recoverable through this component's API.

The fingerprint covers exactly three things: embedding model name, embedding dimensions, and a hash of the chunking config. It does NOT cover the embedding provider or endpoint, any instruction/prompt parameter, or index identity. Two different indexes that happen to store the same fingerprint value are not distinguished -- reusing a vector across indexes is not this gate's concern and is not detected.

Scope BOTH produces the SAME survivors as scope CORPUS: the document pass is subsumed by the corpus pass that follows it. BOTH differs only in that it labels which level collapsed each duplicate ('document' vs 'corpus'). Choosing BOTH buys attribution detail, not a different retention outcome.

Fixed by deriving STORED_FIELDS from IDENTITY_FIELDS + CITATION_FIELDS so a field added to either is stored AND filterable from one place, plus restoring the page range as a real field on the result.

Two defects were self-found by re-reading rather than by tests: (1) IndexWriter.__init__ called validate_payload((), ...), which the shared validator rejects as an empty payload -- construction would have failed on every store; split the configuration checks into _check_config so a misconfigured writer fails at construction with no payload needed.
